info.name: BeePlayer API — Production
info.description:
Complete request coverage for the **BeePlayer** NestJS API in production.

```
https://api.beeplayer1.com
```

The backend mounts no global prefix — controller paths are the URL paths. Interactive Swagger lives at `/api/docs`.

---

### Getting started

1. Select the **BeePlayer — Production** environment (`beeplayer-production.postman_environment.json`) and fill in the credential variables.
2. Run **02 · Auth → Login — admin**. Its test script stores the JWT in `{{token}}` and `{{adminToken}}`.
3. Everything else inherits bearer `{{token}}` unless the request pins a specific role on its Authorization tab.

### Authentication model

There is no single user table. Four Prisma models can authenticate — `Admin`, `Reseller`, `User`, `Customer` — and the JWT payload carries a `type` field that `JwtStrategy.validate()` switches on to pick the right table. Authorization throughout the codebase branches on `user.type`, not on roles.

| Login | Endpoint | Sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Admin / reseller | `POST /auth/login` (email + password) | `{{adminToken}}` / `{{resellerToken}}` |
| Customer | `POST /auth/customer/login` (MAC + key **or** username + password) | `{{customerToken}}` |

The JWT is also accepted as a `token` query or body parameter, not only as a Bearer header — that is what lets `<video src>` and other proxied media requests authenticate.

### Chaining requests

List requests save the first returned id into a collection variable, so the folders run top to bottom without hand-copying ids:

`resellerId` · `customerId` · `playlistId` · `categoryId` · `streamId` · `vodId` · `seriesId` · `episodeId` · `creditPackageId` · `iptvPackageId` · `subscriptionId` · `ticketId` · `transactionId` · `creditRequestId` · `iptvRequestId` · `bankInfoId` · `errorGroupId`

### Things that will trip you up

- **Unknown body fields are rejected.** The global `ValidationPipe` runs with `whitelist` + `forbidNonWhitelisted`, so any property without a matching DTO field returns 400.
- **Every `/customers/iptv/*` route requires `playlist_id`** as a query parameter, and rejects any principal whose `type` is not `customer`.
- **The subscription route is spelled `subcription`.** The typo is consistent across the codebase and is not a bug to route around.
- **`/proxy` and `/video-conversion/*` return media bytes.** Send a `Range` header when testing or Postman will pull down the whole file.
- **Body limit is 50 MB** because bank-transfer receipts are posted as base64 inside JSON.

### Destructive requests

This collection points at production. `DELETE` requests and `PUT /settings/account` operate on live records — check `{{baseUrl}}` before firing them.

exec: // Guard against firing production requests at an unset base URL.
throw new Error('baseUrl is not set — select the BeePlayer environment.');

item.name: 01 · Health & Diagnostics
item.description:
Unauthenticated probes. Use these first to confirm the production API is reachable before debugging auth.

`/customers/test-iptv`, `/customers/test-vod-stream` and `/customers/test-reseller` were removed from the backend: the first two were unauthenticated and carried a live third-party panel username and password in the source, and the third created a real reseller account with a fixed password.

request.description: AppController root. Returns a plain-text greeting.
Reports whether the ffmpeg transcoding pipeline is up.
Diagnostic route that bypasses the JWT guard.
Echoes back the decoded JWT principal -- the fastest way to see what `user.type` the token resolves to.
Swagger UI (HTML). Served by the backend at /api/docs.

item.name: 02 · Auth
item.description:
Single JWT, four principal types (`admin` | `reseller` | `user` | `customer`). The payload carries a `type` field and every downstream service branches on it.

Each login request below saves its token into `{{token}}` (the collection-wide bearer) **and** into a role-specific variable so you can pin a request to one role via its Authorization tab.

request.description: Unified staff login. The service tries the Admin table first, then Reseller. Saves `{{adminToken}}`.
Same endpoint as admin login. Saves `{{resellerToken}}`.

Set-top-box style login. `loginCustomerUnified` accepts **either** macAddress+customerKey **or** username+password. Playlist `pinHash`/`isLocked` are stripped from the response. Saves `{{customerToken}}`.
Web-player style login. Saves `{{customerToken}}`.
Rejected with 403 unless `user.type === "admin"`. `password` must be at least 6 characters.
Returns the record `JwtStrategy.validate()` resolved, plus its `type`. Use it to confirm which table a token authenticates against.

item.name: 03 · Resellers
item.description: Admin-facing reseller administration. The whole controller sits behind `AuthGuard("jwt")`; create/delete additionally require `user.type === "admin"`.

query.description: Lowercase `active` or `suspended`. Resellers have no status column — this maps onto the `isActive` boolean.

request.description: Dashboard aggregate counts.
201 on success. `commissionRate` is a percentage between 0 and 100.
Top up a reseller balance by email rather than id. Writes a Transaction row.
The service tests `status === "active"` (lowercase) and writes `isActive`. **Any other value suspends the reseller**, including `"ACTIVE"` — the comparison is case-sensitive.

item.name: 04 · Users
item.description: Read-only admin view over end-customers, joined with their owning reseller. Whole controller is JWT-guarded.

item.name: 05 · Customers — Management
item.description:
Admin/reseller CRUD over the `Customer` table. A reseller only ever sees its own customers; provisioning spends reseller credit.

**Route-order caveat:** the literal routes (`/customers/stats`, `/customers/playlists/:id`, …) are declared before `/customers/:id`, so they win. Keep that in mind before adding new paths.

request.description:
Send **exactly one** identity pair: `macAddress` + `customerKey` (set-top box) **or** `username` + `password` (web login). Supplying both, or neither, returns 400.

Cost: `subscription.credits` when `subscriptionId` is given, otherwise 1 credit for `creditType: ONE_YEAR` (the default) and 2 for `LIFETIME`. A reseller with too small a balance gets 400 `Insufficient credits`; admins are not charged.

`resellerId` may be supplied by an admin creating on behalf of a reseller.
Scope is derived from the token: admins see all, resellers see their own.
Extends the subscription and debits the reseller credit balance.
Sets a password without knowing the current one. Distinct from the self-service change below.

item.name: 06 · Customers — Account (self)
item.description: Called by the player with a `customer`-type token.

request.description: Channel / movie / series counts across the customer playlists.

item.name: 07 · Customers — Playlists
item.description:
A `Playlist` is one IPTV source: an Xtream Codes panel URL or a raw M3U/M3U8 URL. Everything under the IPTV folders below needs a `playlist_id`.

Playlists can be PIN-locked (`isLocked` + `pinHash`); those two fields are stripped from login responses and the playlist is unlocked with **Verify playlist PIN**.

The `/playlists/*` routes at the end are a backwards-compatible alias kept for older clients — they delegate to the same service methods.

request.description: Older single-playlist accessor kept for legacy clients.
Send `pin` to set/replace the PIN. When a PIN already exists, `currentPin` must match. Send `isLocked: false` with the correct `currentPin` to remove the lock.
Unlocks a PIN-locked playlist for the session.
Shows how the backend parsed the playlist URL into Xtream username/password/host. The first thing to check when a panel returns empty categories.
Backwards-compatible alias. Any `action` other than `verify-pin` returns 400.

item.name: 08 · Customers — Live TV
item.description:
`iptv.service.ts`. These reject any principal whose `type` is not `customer`.

For an Xtream playlist the service derives `player_api.php?username=…&password=…&action=get_live_categories|get_live_streams` from the playlist URL; for a raw M3U it fetches and parses the body line by line. Stream URLs ending in `.hls` are rewritten to `.m3u8` on the way out.

request.description: Pre-`/iptv` channel grouping route retained for older clients.

item.name: 09 · Customers — VOD (Movies)
item.description:
`vod.service.ts`. Same `playlist_id` requirement and the same `.hls` → `.m3u8` rewrite as Live TV.

`/stream` returns the resolved upstream URL; `/proxy` streams the bytes back through the API so an HTTPS page can play an HTTP-only source without tripping the browser mixed-content block.

request.description: Plot, cast, poster, duration — from `get_vod_info`.

header.description: Forwarded upstream so seeking works. Expect a 206 response.

request.description: Streams the movie through the API. Postman will download the body — send a `Range` header to keep the response small while testing.

item.name: 10 · Customers — Series
item.description: `series.service.ts`. Episode listing needs the series id; some raw-M3U playlists also need `series_name` because the parsed entries have no numeric id to key on.

query.description: Needed for raw-M3U playlists where episodes are matched by title

item.name: 11 · Credit Packages & Transactions
item.description:
The admin → reseller half of the credit economy: catalogue, purchases, bank-transfer receipts and the credit-request approval queue.

Bank-transfer receipts are posted as base64 inside JSON, which is why the body parser limit is 50 MB.

**Route-order caveat:** `GET /credit-packages/:id` is declared before the literal `transactions/*` and `credit-requests` routes, so ids that collide with those words will not resolve as you expect.

request.description: Public catalogue — no guard on this route.
Unguarded convenience route so the purchase screen can show where to wire money.
`bankTransferReceipt` is a base64 data URI. Creates a PENDING transaction that an admin then approves.
Rejected with 401 unless `user.type === "reseller"`.
`action` is `approve` or `reject`.
Admin-initiated grant keyed on the reseller email rather than a request id.

item.name: 12 · IPTV Packages & Requests
item.description:
The subscription products a reseller can request for its customers, plus the request/approval queue (`IptvRequest`).

**Route-order caveat:** `GET /iptv-packages/:id` is declared after `test`, `ping`, `stats` and `requests`, so those literals resolve first.

request.description: Public catalogue.
`duration` is in months. `features` is a string array.
Rejected with 401 unless `user.type === "reseller"`.

item.name: 13 · Subscriptions (`subcription`)
item.description:
Subscription plans a customer can be provisioned onto.

The route and module name are misspelled `subcription` throughout the codebase — that is deliberate and consistent; do not "fix" it in a client.

request.description: `duration` is in months; `credits` is what a reseller is charged.

item.name: 14 · Support Tickets
item.description:
Reseller ↔ admin support threads. Resellers see only their own tickets; admins see all and can create on behalf of a reseller via `resellerId`.

Enums — status: `OPEN` `IN_PROGRESS` `RESOLVED` `CLOSED`; priority: `LOW` `MEDIUM` `HIGH` `CRITICAL`; category: `TECHNICAL` `BILLING` `ACCOUNT` `GENERAL`.

item.name: 15 · Bank Information
item.description: Admin-managed bank accounts shown to resellers on the purchase screen. The whole controller is JWT-guarded; `GET /bank-information/active` skips the admin check because the payment screen needs it.

request.description: Promotes one account to the active one. No body.

item.name: 16 · Settings
item.description: Self-service profile for the authenticated principal — works for admin and reseller tokens alike, resolving against whichever table the JWT `type` points to.

request.description: Deletes the authenticated account. Destructive — do not run against production data casually.

item.name: 17 · Activity Logs
item.description: Admin-only audit trail. There is no RolesGuard in this repo, so admin is enforced inline — a reseller token gets a 403.

item.name: 18 · Error Reports
item.description:
`POST /error-reports/ingest` is **public by design**: the most valuable client errors are login and auth failures, which by definition have no valid token. A token is used to attribute the report when present, but a bad one never rejects the request. Abuse is bounded by the throttler (30/min per `deviceId`, 300/min per IP), a 20-event batch cap and a 64 KB body limit.

An unknown field rejects the **whole batch** with 400 — field names are case-sensitive and custom data belongs in `context`.

The read/manage routes below are admin-only: reports carry stack traces and cross-tenant customer identifiers.

See `docs/beeplayer-error-reports.postman_collection.json` for the full field reference and client integration rules.

request.description: Returns 202 `{ "accepted": n }`. Storage is asynchronous.
Identical errors are grouped server-side into one row with a count.

item.name: 19 · Video Conversion (streaming)
item.description:
ffmpeg-backed passthrough/transcode. MKV sources are converted to H.264/AAC MP4 on the fly so iOS can play them; anything else is proxied with `Range` support.

`url` must be **URL-encoded**. These routes use `VideoAuthGuard`, which also accepts the JWT as a `token` query parameter — that is how `<video src>` tags authenticate, since they cannot set an Authorization header.

query.description: Alternative to the Authorization header, for <video src> tags

request.description: Checks whether an upstream URL is reachable from the server. Now behind `VideoAuthGuard` -- it used to be unauthenticated, which made the API a public open proxy. The guard accepts the JWT as a `token` query parameter, so VLC and browser testing still work.

item.name: 20 · Uploads
item.description: Serves stored bank-transfer receipt files. JWT-guarded; content type is inferred from the file extension.

request.description: Replace the filename with the one stored on the transaction record.
